claim: Record lane; no attack; nothing about zeros of zeta. Second referee of the thin prime deletion control: Lemma 1, the repaired Lemma 0 and the tail bounds re-derived; "Lambda_F >= 0, simple real zero at b in (1/2,1)" holds relative to a short-interval prime theorem (Huxley 1972; statement read in two secondary sources, primary text not opened). New numeric cases b = 0.6, 0.85 to 2e7: object not zero and not zeta; exponent 1.0000 at density one; 0.5 at density one half in two directions (branch point). Statement O version 3 written as a new file: line 3 narrowed to {EP, POS, FE, finite order}, lines 1 and 5 and section C rows 1b, 2a rewritten against DEL, previous text kept; count PROVED 4, PROVED-relative 1, MEASURED 1, ARGUED 6. Map: control row DEL, rows P52 and Z33, slot split in Z30, 180 to 182 rows. Engine: three open device types with nodes, control DEL; 1,649 nodes, 8,900 edges, 44,860 generated, 14,980 scored. Scoreboard rerun; FRONTIER text not edited.
errors: No independent referee yet. REFEREE.md is the author's own check (reservations R-1 to R-7). REFEREE2.md in the lane directory is this lane's report on c10-thin-deletion-zero-mode-control (holds, corrections C1 to C6).
surviving: DEL with two referee files, relative to Huxley 1972; half density is a branch point; Tier 0 bounds unconditional, Tier E width relative to an unconfirmed explicit bound; Statement O v3 (c9 file unchanged); map rows DEL, P52, Z33, Z30 addition; engine and scoreboard counts.
lesson: A control proved relative to a classical theorem can get its second referee file, but its label stays "relative to" until the primary text is opened; and a numerical enclosure that rests on an explicit bound must name the bound, since a different published bound changes the width by two orders of magnitude.
